title: Rust: ownership, reliable systems and Arrow data engineering
summary: 48 detailed lessons from first programs through language mechanisms, reliable systems and independently designed projects.

lessons.title: Source, compilation and the first Rust program
lessons.outcome: Model a three-level capacity calculation and explain every intermediate value.
lessons.lab: Compute the capacity of three shelves with eight books each.
lessons.verification: Hello, Rust appears before the lesson marker. The calculated capacity is 24, while addition would give 10.

lessons.title: Bindings, mutability and type inference
lessons.outcome: Choose shadowing or distinct names for parsing stages and justify readability.
lessons.lab: Write a running total with fixed input and mutable accumulator.
lessons.verification: The mutable total changes while the fixed input remains 4. The new count is the text length, not the number twelve.

lessons.title: Integer range, checked arithmetic and numerical intent
lessons.outcome: Choose numeric representation, units and rounding rules for a pricing contract.
lessons.lab: Write a checked quantity-total calculation returning an explicit failure.
lessons.verification: The same boundary produces absence, zero or 255 under three distinct policies. Three items cost 375 cents, while the floating fixture uses an explicit tolerance.

lessons.title: String ownership, UTF-8 and text boundaries
lessons.outcome: Design a text limit and state whether it counts bytes, scalars or graphemes requiring an external library.
lessons.lab: Write a function accepting &str and returning its byte length.
lessons.verification: Both views observe pear while the owner remains usable. The scalar uses two bytes, and its first byte alone is not a valid string slice.

lessons.title: Expressions, branches and exhaustive matches
lessons.outcome: Choose explicit enum matches or a wildcard for a finite application state model.
lessons.lab: Write a negative, zero and positive classifier.
lessons.verification: The branch expression supplies one immutable label. The transition at sixty and the invalid upper range are distinct.

lessons.title: Loops, iterators and termination evidence
lessons.outcome: Design a bounded retry loop and state both its progress measure and its effect policy.
lessons.lab: Implement a first-match search with Option output.
lessons.verification: The borrowed traversal totals twelve and retains the vector. The first match is position one and absence stays explicit.

lessons.title: Functions, return values and contracts
lessons.outcome: Choose owned or borrowed inputs for an API that stores data after the call.
lessons.lab: Write a pure rectangle-area function with a documented valid range.
lessons.verification: The integer remains available after the call. One borrowed interface accepts owned text and a literal.

lessons.title: Ownership, moves and explicit cloning
lessons.outcome: Explain whether a function should borrow, clone or take ownership when retaining data for later use.
lessons.lab: Write a function taking and returning an owned String.
lessons.verification: The new binding owns the text. The cloned String can change independently.

lessons.title: Shared borrowing and scope
lessons.outcome: Choose a borrowed view or owned result for a parser whose caller may discard the input immediately.
lessons.lab: Write a last-word function returning a borrowed slice.
lessons.verification: Two readers coexist and the owner remains intact. The result is a view into caller-owned text, with an explicit empty policy.

lessons.title: Exclusive borrowing and mutation boundaries
lessons.outcome: Design an API that exposes only the smallest mutable region needed by a transformation.
lessons.lab: Write a function swapping the ends of a mutable slice safely.
lessons.verification: The caller retains ownership and observes the deliberate mutation. The two slices mutate separate halves safely.

lessons.title: Slices, arrays and vector growth
lessons.outcome: Choose an array, Vec or slice for stored state, function input and fixed-size coordinates.
lessons.lab: Implement a maximum function accepting a slice and returning Option.
lessons.verification: One slice interface accepts several owning representations. Reserved storage still contains zero logical elements until push.

lessons.title: Structs, methods and validated state
lessons.outcome: Choose a consuming method when an operation should make the prior state unavailable.
lessons.lab: Create a bounded counter with private state and validated operations.
lessons.verification: A successful reservation leaves three units. Excess demand is rejected and zero is an allowed no-op.

lessons.title: Enums and state-specific payloads
lessons.outcome: Design valid transitions between states and explain which transitions should be rejected.
lessons.lab: Model an import as pending, completed or rejected with state-specific information.
lessons.verification: The ready state carries a count rather than an unrelated optional field. Failure preserves its reason and remains a distinct state.

lessons.title: Option and preserving missing information
lessons.outcome: Choose when absence should remain optional and when it should become a domain error.
lessons.lab: Write a first-valid-item lookup returning Option.
lessons.verification: A measured zero remains present and transforms to one. An absent lookup stays absent until the explicit display fallback.

lessons.title: Result, error propagation and recoverable failure
lessons.outcome: Choose a public error enum and explain which internal details should remain private.
lessons.lab: Write a function using ? to compose two fallible steps.
lessons.verification: Malformed text and negative quantity preserve different reasons. Two accepted values and one rejection are accounted for.

lessons.title: Foundation project: a validated inventory report
lessons.outcome: Design a structured import result retaining safe per-record failure categories.
lessons.lab: Render the sorted map with an explicit rejected count.
lessons.verification: Pear totals six and apple totals three. A valid zero remains present while three malformed records are excluded.

lessons.title: Traits and behavioral contracts
lessons.outcome: Choose a trait boundary for a file adapter while keeping the domain core pure.
lessons.lab: Define a small trait for a deterministic formatter.
lessons.verification: The borrowed trait object exposes pricing behavior. The same interface admits an uncapped and capped policy.

lessons.title: Generics, bounds and associated types
lessons.outcome: Choose a generic parameter or associated type for a producer relationship and explain who selects it.
lessons.lab: Create a generic pair that swaps owned elements.
lessons.verification: The same function returns an integer or owned String. The iterator's item relationship supports a typed sum.

lessons.title: Lifetime parameters and borrowed API design
lessons.outcome: Choose a borrowed or owned result for a cache boundary and justify cost and lifetime.
lessons.lab: Write a borrowed prefix parser with the narrowest lifetime relationship.
lessons.verification: The output is a borrowed view of the longer input. The independent owned result survives the temporary scope.

lessons.title: Iterators, laziness and consumption
lessons.outcome: Choose iter, iter_mut or into_iter for three operations and justify ownership.
lessons.lab: Write a borrowed transformation returning a collected result.
lessons.verification: The recipe selects and transforms while retaining the borrowed source. The iterator advances and eventually exhausts.

lessons.title: Closures and Fn capability bounds
lessons.outcome: Choose capture ownership for work that will run on another thread.
lessons.lab: Implement a helper accepting FnMut for repeated transformations.
lessons.verification: The closure updates its borrowed accumulator before the borrow ends. The closure transfers its captured String to the caller once.

lessons.title: Custom errors and preserving causes
lessons.outcome: Choose which layer translates an internal error into a public response and what context it may expose.
lessons.lab: Define a custom error for an importer with syntax and storage boundaries.
lessons.verification: Negative and malformed inputs remain separate variants. The message explains the rule without repeating raw input.

lessons.title: Modules, visibility and a stable public surface
lessons.outcome: Split a future library and executable crate by responsibility and document dependency direction.
lessons.lab: Move a pure domain operation into an inline module.
lessons.verification: The consumer uses the domain module interface. The shorter imported name refers to the same function.

lessons.title: Tests, assertions and useful counterexamples
lessons.outcome: Separate unit, integration, compile-fail and runtime evidence for a library change.
lessons.lab: Write table-driven checks for a quantity validator.
lessons.verification: Negative, zero and positive cases satisfy the stated clamp rule. Zero rejects the incorrect default while idempotence adds a second property.

lessons.title: Files, bytes and owned cleanup
lessons.outcome: Design cleanup on every failure path using a small owned temporary-resource wrapper.
lessons.lab: Create an owned temporary-file round trip for a report.
lessons.verification: The Unicode text round-trips and the owned path is removed. Valid UTF-8 decodes while an invalid byte sequence is rejected.

lessons.title: Maps, sets and algorithmic cost
lessons.outcome: Compare repeated linear membership checks with a built index, including construction and memory costs.
lessons.lab: Build a deterministic frequency report.
lessons.verification: Duplicate b accumulates and output keys are sorted. The set reports a duplicate without creating a second entry.

lessons.title: Scoped threads and explicit joins
lessons.outcome: Choose threads or sequential work using workload size and synchronization cost.
lessons.lab: Build a scoped parallel computation returning values to the parent.
lessons.verification: The borrowed input remains usable after the joined scope. The parent combines two completed results.

lessons.title: Arc, Mutex and compound shared invariants
lessons.outcome: Choose message passing or shared locking for a service and justify the invariant owner.
lessons.lab: Implement a locked bounded reservation operation.
lessons.verification: All four hundred increments are retained. The transfer preserves the total under one protected tuple.

lessons.title: Channels, backpressure and completion
lessons.outcome: Choose blocking, rejection or intentional dropping for a workload and explain producer evidence.
lessons.lab: Build a bounded producer-consumer report pipeline.
lessons.verification: One item is admitted and the next immediate send reports full capacity. The receiver drains both values and ends after the sender is dropped.

lessons.title: Send, Sync and type-driven concurrency safety
lessons.outcome: Document why a proposed custom type is or is not Send and Sync from its members.
lessons.lab: Choose a safe shared-state type for a small concurrent counter.
lessons.verification: Owned text crosses the thread boundary and returns its length. The compiler accepts the declared safe capability combinations.

lessons.title: Box, Rc, Weak and recursive structures
lessons.outcome: Choose Box, Rc or Arc for unique, local-shared and cross-thread ownership scenarios.
lessons.lab: Model a parent-child relationship with a weak back-reference.
lessons.verification: Box makes the recursive type have a finite outer size. The weak reference does not keep the String alive.

lessons.title: Composition project: a reusable inventory library
lessons.outcome: Design a second adapter that reuses the same validated library without copying its implementation.
lessons.lab: Build and test InventoryLab through its documented Cargo commands.
lessons.verification: The report accumulates duplicates and orders keys. Two invalid rows are counted and a valid zero remains present.

lessons.title: Futures, async syntax and executor boundaries
lessons.outcome: Plan a separately prepared Tokio service, naming runtime, cancellation, I/O and dependency requirements.
lessons.lab: Explain the ownership responsibilities of an executor in a written event trace.
lessons.verification: The immediately ready future yields seven on its first poll. The pending future reports no completed value.

lessons.title: Unsafe code, FFI and a documented safety argument
lessons.outcome: Design an FFI ownership document stating allocation, release, encoding and error conventions.
lessons.lab: Write a safe wrapper specification before considering an unsafe implementation.
lessons.verification: The reconstructed view matches the live initialized array. A normal slice provides the same read contract without a manual safety burden.

lessons.title: Memory layout, allocation and performance evidence
lessons.outcome: Choose a layout for repeated column scans and explain locality, ownership and update tradeoffs.
lessons.lab: Write a benchmark plan comparing repeated clone with borrowed processing.
lessons.verification: String handle size is equal while the owned text lengths differ. Only ten initialized elements participate in the sum.

lessons.title: Cargo, editions and reproducible release workflows
lessons.outcome: Design a dependency upgrade review including lock diff, licenses, compile tests and runtime evidence.
lessons.lab: Run its tests and inspect a deliberately changed public contract.
lessons.verification: Edition and compiler version remain different policy fields. One failed gate prevents a claimed complete release.

lessons.title: Arrow columnar memory and typed arrays
lessons.outcome: Compare row-object and columnar representations for a repeated analytical scan.
lessons.lab: Construct paired integer and text columns with equal row counts.
lessons.verification: The concrete column contains three non-null integers. Different text lengths share one logical column.

lessons.title: Arrow nulls, validity and NaN semantics
lessons.outcome: Define missingness and non-finite policies for a sensor dataset before calculating a mean.
lessons.lab: Write a summary returning valid, null and finite counts.
lessons.verification: A valid zero and a null remain distinct positions. The column contains one null, one present NaN and one finite value.

lessons.title: Schemas, fields and RecordBatch invariants
lessons.outcome: Design a schema evolution policy that preserves names, units and saved data meaning.
lessons.lab: Construct a batch for a small validated inventory dataset.
lessons.verification: Two aligned columns form a two-row, two-column batch. Unequal column lengths are rejected.

lessons.title: Compute kernels, filtering and row selection
lessons.outcome: Choose filter or take for a sampling procedure and explain duplicate-row consequences.
lessons.lab: Filter every column of a batch consistently under one row mask.
lessons.verification: Filtering retains two and six in input order. Take repeats and reorders values according to the index sequence.

lessons.title: Variable-width arrays, nested values and zero-copy slices
lessons.outcome: Explain when retaining a tiny shared slice may retain excessive memory and when copying is justified.
lessons.lab: Build a nested column from a small ragged dataset.
lessons.verification: The three rows are a two-child list, an empty list and a null list. The sliced array exposes middle at its logical index zero.

lessons.title: Arrow IPC and explicit stream completion
lessons.outcome: Design an IPC transport with size limits, schema checks and explicit ownership of received buffers.
lessons.lab: Build an in-memory IPC round trip preserving a nullable column.
lessons.verification: The schema and two values round-trip as one complete batch. Arbitrary bytes are rejected as an IPC stream.

lessons.title: CSV and JSON readers with explicit schemas
lessons.outcome: Design an inference-to-reviewed-schema workflow with checks for later type and nullability drift.
lessons.lab: Read a small nullable dataset and validate its domain ranges afterward.
lessons.verification: The parser produces two rows under the explicit schema. JSON null becomes Arrow null under the declared nullable field.

lessons.title: Cross-language data contracts: decimals, timestamps and metadata
lessons.outcome: Plan a separately prepared Rust-to-PyArrow IPC round trip that checks schema, nulls, decimal scale and timestamp units in both languages.
lessons.lab: Create a schema documenting measurement units and timestamp precision.
lessons.verification: Coefficient 125 with scale two represents 1.25 under the declared contract. The second value is one thousand milliseconds after the epoch.

lessons.title: Bounded batch pipelines and data accounting
lessons.outcome: Design cancellation and partial-output semantics for a long-running import.
lessons.lab: Apply the same accounting to an Arrow batch reader.
lessons.verification: Three chunks account for five rows and total fifteen. Valid zero is retained and every input row is accounted for.

lessons.title: Diagnostics, security boundaries and safe output
lessons.outcome: Design a fixed-operation boundary that separates validated data from executable instructions.
lessons.lab: Instrument an importer with submitted, accepted and rejected counts.
lessons.verification: The event retains useful context without echoing input contents. Only explicitly listed actions are admitted.

lessons.title: Properties, compile-fail cases and regression design
lessons.outcome: Design an external fuzzing and compile-fail plan with reproducible seeds, minimized failures and clear acceptance scope.
lessons.lab: Write a property checking an Arrow filter's output count against its Boolean mask.
lessons.verification: One hundred bounded pairs satisfy the addition relation. Sorting establishes order without losing the repeated three.

lessons.title: Capstone: a validated Arrow analytical report
lessons.outcome: Deliver a project README with schema, ownership, bounds, failure policies, actual runtime evidence and one independent Arrow extension.
lessons.lab: Build a multi-column RecordBatch report and round-trip it through IPC.
lessons.verification: Three valid nonnegative values total five, alongside one null and one rejected negative. No submitted rows and two missing observations remain different reports.
